request: How is the Highway Trust Fund financed, and when is it projected to run short of money?

reply.reply:
**The Highway Trust Fund is funded primarily by fuel taxes, and its combined accounts are projected to run a shortfall by the end of 2028.**

- CBO's February 2026 baseline projects a combined HTF end-of-year shortfall of $19.55 billion in 2028. (R47573, PDF p. 12)
- The Fund is primarily financed by federal gasoline and diesel taxes, allocated between its highway and mass transit accounts. (R48472, PDF p. 6)
- Fuel taxes make up roughly 85% of annual highway-account revenue, with gasoline and diesel taxes contributing about 60% and 25%, respectively. (R48472, PDF p. 6)
reply.reasoning: CRS finds gasoline and diesel taxes account for roughly 85% of Highway Account revenue. CBO's February 2026 baseline, reported by CRS, projects the combined balance becomes negative in 2028, with an end-of-year shortfall of $19.55 billion.
